description: A feature flag read inside the ad service's `GetAds` handler activated a singleton `CPULoad` that spawned 4 daemon threads each running a tight `Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis())` loop; the threads pinned CPU cores and saturated container CPU and `jvm_cpu_recent_utilization_ratio` on the `ad` service.
mechanism: The flag is read in [`AdService.java#L172`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/AdService.java#L172): on every `getAds` gRPC call, `CPULoad.getInstance().execute()` is invoked with the boolean value of the `adHighCpu` flag. When the flag is `true`, [`CPULoad.java#L46-L52`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L46) calls `spawnLoadWorkers(4)`, which launches 4 daemon threads ([`CPULoad.java#L64-L74`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L64)). Each thread runs a tight `while(shouldRun) { Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()); }` loop ([`CPULoad.java#L101-L103`](../../opentelemetry-demo/src/ad/src/main/java/oteldemo/problempattern/CPULoad.java#L101)), saturating CPU cores with continuous logarithm calculations. The threads persist until the flag is toggled off, at which point `stopWorkers()` sets `shouldRun=false` on each thread. Because the workers are spawned only once (guarded by the `running` flag at line 49), repeated `getAds` calls while the flag is on do not create additional threads.

variants.description: Ad container total CPU usage rate (nanoseconds/sec) spiked from ~2e6 to ~3.9e9, reflecting the 4 CPU-bound daemon threads consuming nearly 4 full cores
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~1.7-2.1e+06. At 14:09 UTC (one minute after incident), the value jumps to 7.14e+08 (~430x baseline), marking the clear onset of the CPU spike.

variants.description: Ad container usermode CPU usage rate spiked from ~1.5e6 to ~3.9e9 ns/s, as the Logarithmizer threads run entirely in user space computing Math.log() in tight loops
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~1.2-1.5e+06. At 14:09, one minute after the incident marker, the value jumps to ~7.12e+08 — roughly 500x the baseline — clearly the first timestamp of the spike. By 14:10 it reaches ~2.83e+09 and stabilizes around ~3.9e+09.

variants.description: Host-level CPU idle utilization ratio dropped from ~0.87 to ~0.37 as the ad container's CPU-saturating threads consumed available idle CPU capacity across the host
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident the idle CPU ratio oscillates around ~0.875. At 14:08 it is still at 0.886, then at 14:09 it drops sharply to 0.790 and by 14:10 collapses to ~0.37 where it stays. The last timestamp showing normal pre-incident activity is 14:08, marking the onset of the collapse.

variants.description: flagd impression counter for adHighCpu with result variant 'on' incremented after the flag was enabled, confirming the CPU load problem pattern was activated.
variants.onset_reasoning: The metric is flat at 0 through 14:08 (incident time). At 14:09 it jumps to 0.00416667, which is the first non-zero value and clearly the start of the spike above baseline.

variants.description: Ad container CPU utilization ratio spiked from ~0.16 to ~395 because the adHighCpu flag spawned 4 tight-loop Logarithmizer threads saturating CPU cores inside the ad container
variants.onset_reasoning: Pre-incident baseline is ~0.15-0.19. At 14:09 the value jumps to 381.683, a ~2000x increase from baseline, clearly marking the spike onset.

logs.name: ad: High CPU-Load problempattern enabled (INFO)
logs.description: At 14:08:31.239 UTC, the ad service emitted 26 INFO logs announcing that the High CPU-Load problem pattern had been enabled.
logs.cause: Smoking-gun direct evidence of the adHighCpu flag. On every getAds invocation, AdService.java:172 calls ffClient.getBooleanValue("adHighCpu", false, ctx) and passes the result to CPULoad.execute(enabled). When enabled=true, CPULoad.java:48 logs "High CPU-Load problempattern enabled" at INFO and, if not already running, spawns 4 daemon Logarithmizer threads (CPULoad.java:50, 64-73) that tight-loop Math.log(System.currentTimeMillis()) to saturate CPU. Note the log is not an error — the ad service continues serving requests successfully, just under CPU pressure.
logs.source: ad service (Java, oteldemo.problempattern.CPULoad logger via OpenTelemetry Java agent)
